sentences.text: Both species of Susisuchus share a specific skull feature where the squamosal and parietal bones meet at the posterior border of the supratemporal fenestra.
The animal possessed a dorsal shield of osteoderms similar to those found in modern crocodilians and the derived clade Eusuchia.
Susisuchus was among the first mesoeucrocodylians to evolve a tetraserial paravertebral shield made of dorsal osteoderms that made the back more rigid.
A tetraserial paravertebral shield consists of four separate rows of osteoderms near the midline of the back.
In this species, two rows of large osteoderms segment into four smaller ones, accompanied by two rows of accessory osteoderms on each side that did not form part of the main shield.
S. anatoceps was the first crocodyliform described from the Crato Formation in the Araripe Basin.
Researchers believe the holotype specimen was a desiccated carcass before burial and fossilization.
The animal was likely restricted to a maximum size of 50 kg because larger bodies would have exceeded the structural limits of its high-walking posture.
Susisuchus was an extinct crocodyliform that lived in Brazil during the Early Cretaceous period, specifically from the Berriasian to the Aptian stages between 143.1 and 113.2 million years ago.
The genus Susisuchus was named in 2003 by Salisbury et al. and is the only member of its family, Susisuchidae.

Fossils of the primary species have been found in the Nova Olinda Member of the Aptian-age Crato Formation in northeastern Brazil, while a second species, S. jaguaribensis, was named in 2009 based on fragmentary remains.
The remains of S. jaguaribensis were found about 115 km from the discovery site of S. anatoceps in the Lima Campos Basin.
A 2009 specimen from the Crato Formation was tentatively classified as cf. Susisuchus sp. based on unique fibula and leg bone proportions.
There are currently 5 recorded fossil occurrences of Susisuchus known to science.
The segmented paravertebral shield allowed Susisuchus greater lateral flexibility in its trunk.
This flexibility likely enabled efficient lateral undulation swimming in the animal, resulting in greater locomotion efficiency.
Susisuchus is closely related to the genera Pachycheilosuchus from Glen Rose, Texas, USA, and Isisfordia from Winton, Queensland, Australia.
Susisuchus is placed outside the Eusuchia clade as its sister taxon, unlike its relative Isisfordia.
The animal possessed amphicoelus vertebrae, meaning the ends of its vertebrae are concave, a trait found in the thoracic, lumbar, and caudal regions.
The combination of amphicoelus vertebrae and a tetraserial shield is unique enough to define the family Susisuchidae, of which Susisuchus is the only member.
Susisuchus was an extinct crocodyliform that lived in Brazil during the Early Cretaceous period.
